summary: Kavach MTTR flywheel — honest agent processing times vs modeled human baseline
method: Agent MTTR is measured from StubLLM timeline processing_ms (sum per run; see backend/app/flywheel/mttr.py and backend/app/events/metrics/mttr.jsonl). Speedup vs human is a modeled comparison against a cited human baseline — not live OpenAI wall-clock. Full real-LLM re-record deferred (OPENAI_API_KEY present but recording pass skipped as heavy).

honesty.notes: StubLLM uses the same short-circuit processing_ms for every scenario (first ≈3.0s, repeat-with-prior ≈0.2s). That ratio is real for the stub path but must not be sold as identical real-LLM wall-clock across all four scenarios. Human baseline is a literature midpoint, not a Kavach A/B study.

human_baseline.label: modeled
human_baseline.citation: Conservative 30-minute midpoint for retail data-quality on-call triage before a fix lands (common industry range ~15–45 minutes; cf. PagerDuty State of Digital Operations / typical DQ incident anecdotes). Not measured in this repo.
human_baseline.source: modeled midpoint — not a Kavach controlled study
